title: Blaze Solution Card (MVP subset)
description: MVP subset of the Solution Card defined in research/04-retrieval-architecture.md §1. Deliberately written without $ref/$defs/anyOf so that (a) the hand-rolled validator in validate.ts stays dependency-free and (b) a simplified copy can be handed to `claude --json-schema` for structured output. Body budget: 400-1200 tokens as rendered by renderCardBody() in validate.ts.

id.description: Stable slug. MUST equal the card's filename without the .json extension so that `GET /cards/:id` resolves by filename.

status.description: Cards in packages/cards/ are loaded by the gateway. Cards in packages/cards/candidates/ are `candidate` and are only loaded once promoted by moving the file up one directory.

replay.description: Replay-grade card: produced by a verified run of THIS task on THIS stack, so solution.code_snippets[] hold FULL final file contents and solution.commands[] the non-file edits. Body budget is REPLAY_TOKEN_BUDGET_MAX, not the 1200-token distilled budget.

title.description: Short problem-shaped phrase. Convention: lowercase kebab-case, e.g. `stripe-webhook-signature-fails-on-reparsed-body`.

trigger.description: Third person. States what the card does AND when to use it. Budget matches the Agent Skills `description` limit of 1024 chars.

anti_trigger.description: The negative boundary: 2-5 superficially similar problems for which this card is the WRONG answer, each saying where to go instead.

problem_signature.description: Verbatim symptom strings a future agent will actually search with: error text, log lines, observed behaviour. Not abstractions.

context_fingerprint.description: Structured stack filter. Extra keys (runtime, package_manager, repo_shape, os, fingerprint_hash) are allowed and ignored by the MVP gateway.

frameworks.description: Boosted at retrieval time when `name` intersects the stack detected from the caller's cwd.

name.description: npm package name as it appears in package.json dependencies.

range.description: semver range the lesson is known to apply to, e.g. ">=16.0.0 <17.0.0".

version.description: Exact version observed in the originating run.

procedure.description: Ordered steps, each classified by degrees of freedom. `exact` = reproduce verbatim, do not paraphrase. `templated` = keep the shape, substitute the names. `heuristic` = judgement call, adapt to the repo.

pitfalls.description: Capped at 3 (ReasoningBank's item cap). Pitfall 1 MUST be the exact non-obvious gotcha, stated plainly. Target <=32 words per pitfall; validate.ts warns beyond that.

code_snippets.description: One variabilized exemplar is the target. Non-fixed elements should be replaced with descriptive names, not the originating repo's identifiers. A distilled card is capped at 3 snippets (enforced by validate.ts); the higher maxItems exists only for replay cards, which carry every file the verified run wrote.

content.description: A distilled card carries a fragment; a replay card carries the whole file, hence the generous cap. The rendered-body budget is the real limit.

commands.description: Edits that are not whole files: a package.json script addition, a codemod invocation. Applied in order, after the snippets are written.

evidence.description: What was actually observed, for a card whose solution has been run: verified_at, verify_script, verify_output.

origin_repo_note.description: How the card was obtained, and on what repo. The literal value `decoy-for-threshold-testing` marks a card that exists only as a retrieval negative.

keywords.description: Lexical retrieval surface. Include package names, file conventions, API identifiers and version numbers.
